definitions.explanation: A staged dramatic work in which much or all of the text is sung, with orchestral accompaniment. Includes both individual works and the genre as a whole.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}はオペラが{大好|だいす}きだ。
{昨夜|さくや}、{有名|ゆうめい}なオペラを{観|み}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: Last night I went to see a famous opera.

examples.japanese: イタリア{語|ご}のオペラは{字幕|じまく}があった{方|ほう}が{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: Italian operas are easier to enjoy with subtitles.

notes:
From Italian "opera." The Japanese word covers both individual works and the genre. Often paired with verbs like {観|み}る (to watch) or {聴|き}く (to listen to).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- オペラを{観|み}る: to see an opera
- オペラ{歌手|かしゅ}: opera singer
- オペラ{座|ざ}: opera house (パリオペラ{座|ざ}: Paris Opera)
- {本格|ほんかく}オペラ: a full-scale opera production

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ミュージカル: musical — songs alternate with spoken dialogue; lighter style
- {歌劇|かげき}: literal Japanese translation "sung drama"; mostly used in formal/written contexts and proper names ({宝塚|たからづか}{歌劇団|かげきだん})
